findings.description: The actor-equality check (`github.actor == github.event.pull_request.user.login`) is ANDed across the whole `pull_request` branch, so it also gates `ready_for_review`, not just `synchronize` as the adjacent comment's rationale describes. GitHub permits any repo writer to mark another contributor's draft PR ready for review, which sets `github.actor` to the writer while `pull_request.user.login` remains the original author, failing this branch for that PR. The gap is non-blocking in practice because the same comment documents the intended fallback ('To review someone else's PR, comment `@claude review` on it'), which uses the separate `issue_comment` branch and isn't subject to this check.

`fromJSON('["OWNER", "MEMBER", "COLLABORATOR"]')` is duplicated verbatim across both branches of the template's `if:` block. A prior review called this not actionable because `env` isn't available in job-level `if:` — true, but `vars` is (this very file already reads `vars.CLAUDE_REVIEW_ENABLED` at job level), so a repo/org Actions variable could dedupe the list. That alternative is a worse tradeoff here: it would move a security-relevant allowlist out of versioned YAML into mutable dashboard config, unaudited by git history. With occurrences ~4 lines apart and `test/workflow-sync.test.ts` pinning both independently, duplication remains the pragmatic choice, not an oversight — worth revisiting only if a third trust check is added.

The `TRANSFORMS` regex that locates the template's owner-gate block to replace it (`/    # Only the repository's owner, members of the organisation[\s\S]*?author_association\)\)\n/`) uses a non-greedy wildcard that crosses newlines, unlike every sibling transform in the same array, which stays fully literal or bounded to one line. It matches correctly today (only one `author_association))` occurrence exists), but a future edit adding an earlier `author_association))` sequence could make it silently match a shorter span instead of failing loudly like the script's own stated invariant intends. Backstopped by the exact-equality sync test and explicit substring assertions, so a bad render would likely still surface as a failing test.
